The Auto merge loop now does the work itself instead of only listing
Lore's own pull requests. With the loop switched on, every open pull
request that code review has passed, whoever opened it, gets one
`auto-merge` run on the external floor. The run waits until CI is green,
no review thread is open, Lore's review stands approved on the head and
the pull request has been open for the minimum age. Red CI, a conflict
or open review goes to a new `auto-merge-fix` agent, which pushes
commits without rewriting history and answers each thread; its replies
are posted in the threads and the settled ones resolved, three rounds at
most. Then the `approve` station approves it, as the lore-reviewer App
when it is installed (#3307) and as Lore's own App otherwise. On a
branch whose rule asks for an app…

The Auto merge loop now does the work itself instead of only listing Lore's own pull requests. With the loop switched on, every open pull request that code review has passed, whoever opened it, gets one `auto-merge` run on the external floor. The run waits until CI is green, no review thread is open, Lore's review stands approved on the head and the pull request has been open for the minimum age. Red CI, a conflict or open review goes to a new `auto-merge-fix` agent, which pushes commits without rewriting history and answers each thread; its replies are posted in the threads and the settled ones resolved, three rounds at most. Then the `approve` station approves it, as the lore-reviewer App when it is installed (#3307) and as Lore's own App otherwise. On a branch whose rule asks for an app…

# Feature Specification: Lore merges on protected repos, and every PR knows what blocks it

## lore-reviewer App and the auto-merge loop

The `auto-merge` line (`libs/assembly-lines/src/floor-pipelines/auto-merge.yaml`, one run per `pr_url`) waits at `await-merge`, a human station the `pr-ready-check` sweep answers, and fixes nothing *(amended 2026-10-23: the `auto-merge-fix` agent with its `fix-pr` and `fix-replies` stations is gone; a loop pull request is rebased and repaired by the implementation loop on the pull request's own events, `specs/external-floor` FR12.19, and a person's pull request is the person's to fix)*. Each of these holds the wait, in order: a conflict or red CI; an open review thread, whether or not a review, re-check or reply run is still answering it; Lore's review n…

## What Changed

- `auto-merge.yaml` is `await-merge → approve → done`. The `auto-merge-fix` agent, its `fix-pr` and `fix-replies` stations, the review feedback the wait built for it and the `any`-review branch of `postReply` are deleted. `decideMergeReady` answers ready or wait; a red, conflicted or thread-blocked pull request is waited out.
- `decidePrReady` (`await-pr`) reads GitHub's mergeability and how many commits of main the branch lacks, the count `loop-sync-check` reads, before CI: conflict → `pr_conflicting`, behind → `pr_behind`, both `changes_requested`, which the line routes to `sync-pr`. The sync edges get `iteration_max: 6`; the fix keeps 3.
- `libs/shared/src/work/backlog/loop-pr-upkeep.ts`: a settled loop pull request that is behind, conflicted or red gets an **upkeep run…

## What Changed

- `auto-merge.yaml` is `await-merge → approve → done`. The
`auto-merge-fix` agent, its `fix-pr` and `fix-replies` stations, the
review feedback the wait built for it and the `any`-review branch of
`postReply` are deleted. `decideMergeReady` answers ready or wait; a
red, conflicted or thread-blocked pull request is waited out.
- `decidePrReady` (`await-pr`) reads GitHub's mergeability and how many
commits of main the branch lacks, the count `loop-sync-check` reads,
before CI: conflict → `pr_conflicting`, behind → `pr_behind`, both
`changes_requested`, which the line routes to `sync-pr`. The sync edges
get `iteration_max: 6`; the fix keeps 3.
- `libs/shared/src/work/backlog/loop-pr-upkeep.ts`: a settled loop pull
request that is behind, conflicted or red gets an **upkeep run…

## Why

The implementation loop looked after its pull request only while its run
was open. The run parks at `await-pr`, which the `pr-ready-check` sweep
polls every two minutes, and the moment the pull request is green with
no open thread the run ends so the backlog slot frees. From then on
nothing of the loop watched the pull request: when main moved the branch
fell behind or conflicted, when main's CI changed the branch went red,
and the ticket's pull request sat there. The auto-merge loop (#3320) had
grown a fixer to cover this, `auto-merge-fix`, which merged the base in
and edited any author's branch. That is not its job: auto merge waits
and approves, and the loop that opened a pull request keeps it
mergeable.

Two smaller holes while the run was parked: `await-pr` never read
mergeabi…

PR re-cinq/lore#3376 (2026-10-23): the implementation loop keeps its pull requests mergeable on GitHub events; auto merge fixes nothing.

DECISIONS (user): auto-merge must not fix anything — `auto-merge-fix`, `fix-pr`, `fix-replies` deleted, `decideMergeReady` answers ready|wait only; a loop PR is the loop's to rebase/repair, a person's PR is the person's. Rebase whenever a loop PR is behind main, not only when red.

This was raised in review on #1942 and I merged before reading the thread, so it lands as a follow-up rather than an amend. The same review also claimed `decideCiReady` wrongly returns ready when mergeability is null and CI passed. That one I disagree with: null means GitHub has not finished computing mergeability, and if checks exist and are green then the branch built, which is the only question this wait asks. Mergeability matters at the end-of-line wait, where the pull request is actually merged.
